source: From API Call to ESG Disclosure: Connecting EcoLogits Data to ISO/IEC TR 20226 and Corporate Sustainability Reporting

metrics.plain: the electricity each AI request uses in the data center, including cooling and building overhead
metrics.computation: GPU energy (ML.ENERGY regression) + server overhead, multiplied by PUE

metrics.plain: the electricity used by the graphics processors that generate the answer
metrics.computation: E_GPU = (alpha x P_active + beta) x tokens_out

metrics.plain: how much extra electricity a data center uses beyond the computers themselves; 1.10 means 10 percent overhead
litres of water consumed per unit of electricity, on site for cooling and off site to generate the power
metrics.computation: On-site provider WUE plus off-site WRI factor

metrics.plain: the greenhouse-gas emissions of each request, and of each 1,000 words of output
metrics.computation: GWP per request and per 1,000 output tokens

metrics.iso_name: Carbon intensity of an ML model
metrics.plain: the grams of CO2e each 1,000 words of output costs the planet
metrics.computation: Total GWP per request divided by tokens_out

metrics.plain: operating plus hardware emissions for one unit of useful work, here one request
metrics.computation: Operational R plus embodied R, per functional unit

metrics.plain: emissions from generating the electricity the requests used
the share of emissions from manufacturing the servers and GPUs, spread over their working life
metrics.ghg_protocol: Scope 3 Cat 1 for API/SaaS, Cat 2 if we own GPUs

metrics.plain: how much the hardware and electricity draw down scarce minerals and metals
metrics.computation: Energy x ADEME ADPe factor plus embodied ADPe

metrics.plain: all the energy drawn from nature to supply the electricity and hardware, including fuel extraction
metrics.computation: Energy x primary-energy factor plus embodied PE

metrics.plain: water consumed to cool the data center and to generate its electricity
metrics.computation: On-site cooling WUE plus off-site generation WUE
metrics.posture: Report with caveat, E3 not E1

metrics.plain: the written explanation of how these figures were produced and what they leave out

EcoLogits does not evaluate model quality or accuracy

not_calculable.iso_name: Supply chain metrics (mines, smelters, material hazard, community)

glossary.name: Abiotic Depletion Potential for elements
glossary.definition: Depletion of scarce minerals and metals, in kilograms of antimony equivalent.
glossary.esg_status: Not required by any ESG standard today; internal only.

glossary.name: Primary energy
glossary.definition: All energy drawn from nature, including fuel extraction, to supply the activity.
glossary.esg_status: GRI 302-2 with caveat; never added to emissions.

glossary.name: Water Usage Effectiveness
glossary.definition: Litres of water consumed per kilowatt-hour of electricity.

glossary.name: Power Usage Effectiveness
glossary.definition: Total data-center electricity divided by the electricity the computers use.

glossary.name: Water Consumption Footprint
glossary.definition: Water consumed on site for cooling plus off site for electricity generation.
glossary.esg_status: ESRS E3-3, E3-5 and GRI 303-3, with caveat.

glossary.name: Software Carbon Intensity
glossary.definition: Operating plus embodied emissions per unit of useful work (ISO/IEC 21031:2024).

glossary.name: Global Warming Potential
glossary.definition: Greenhouse-gas emissions expressed as grams of CO2 equivalent (gCO2e).

glossary.name: Tonnes of CO2 equivalent
glossary.definition: Greenhouse-gas emissions in metric tonnes; 1 tonne = 1,000,000 grams.

copy.scope3_cat1: AI API calls are purchased services. They belong in Category 1 (Purchased Goods and Services), not Category 4 (Upstream Transportation). Confirm your classification with your ESG lead.
copy.location_based: These figures use national average grid mixes. If your provider supplies market-based data from power purchase agreements, that is a separate figure we do not calculate.
copy.energy_placement: Energy from AI API services is Scope 3, not your own operations. It feeds GRI 302-2, not the ESRS E1-5 numerator, unless you operate your own GPU fleet.
copy.water_placement: Water maps to ESRS E3, not E1. On-site and off-site are reported separately. Water used to manufacture the hardware is not included.
copy.pe_double_count: Primary energy includes upstream fuel extraction. Report it under GRI 302-2. Do not add it to the emissions figure; it is a different measure of the same activity.
copy.adpe: No ESG standard currently requires this. We track it internally for future EU Critical Raw Materials Act work and raw-material due diligence.
copy.estimate_tier: These are Average-data estimates under the GHG Protocol hierarchy: physical and token-based, materially more accurate than spend-based estimation, and defensible as a reasonable estimate under AR 40 when the limitations are disclosed.
copy.supplier_precedence: Where your provider publishes its own figures, those take precedence. We keep our estimate alongside as a cross-check and record any discrepancy.
copy.long_context: This team's prompts are much longer than its outputs. Prompt-processing energy is not yet modelled, so these figures likely understate actual consumption.
